questions.title: A band is a numbered stretch
questions.text: Radio waves wiggle at different speeds. A band is a stretch of those speeds with a number for a name, like a lane on a road. We count the speed in MHz (megahertz). B71 sits low on the ruler: its downlink runs from {band:B71.dl_low_mhz} to {band:B71.dl_high_mhz} MHz. n258 sits far up at {band:n258.dl_low_mhz} MHz.

questions.title: B is 4G, n is 5G
questions.text: A band that starts with "B" is 4G (also called LTE). A band that starts with "n" is 5G (also called NR). B71 and n71 are twins: they use exactly the same space ({band:B71.dl_low_mhz} to {band:B71.dl_high_mhz} MHz downlink).

questions.prompt: Which is the higher frequency, 2000 MHz or 2 GHz?
questions.why: 1 GHz (gigahertz) is 1000 MHz, so 2 GHz is 2000 MHz. Same thing, different units.

questions.prompt: Your phone shows "n71". Is that 4G or 5G?

questions.why: B66's downlink starts at {band:B66.dl_low_mhz} MHz. B71's starts at {band:B71.dl_low_mhz} MHz.

questions.title: Three parts of the ruler
questions.text: In this app, we split the ruler in three. Low band is any band that starts below 1000 MHz, like B71 ({band:B71.dl_low_mhz} MHz). High band is the very top, called mmWave, like n260 ({band:n260.dl_low_mhz} MHz). Mid band is everything in between, like B2 ({band:B2.dl_low_mhz} MHz). Other people draw the lines a bit differently, so this is the app's own rule.

questions.title: Reach versus speed
questions.text: Low bands are like a deep voice: they travel far and get through walls, but carry less. High bands are like a whisper that moves lots of data: very fast, but they stop at the first wall. Mid bands are in the middle.

questions.title: Uplink and downlink
questions.text: Uplink is your phone talking to the tower (up). Downlink is the tower talking to your phone (down). Think of a phone call: you speak, then you listen.

questions.title: FDD and TDD
questions.text: FDD is a road with two lanes: one for up, one for down. B2 is FDD: uplink {band:B2.ul_low_mhz} to {band:B2.ul_high_mhz} MHz, downlink {band:B2.dl_low_mhz} to {band:B2.dl_high_mhz} MHz. TDD is a single lane where up and down take turns, very fast. n41 is TDD: one range, {band:n41.dl_low_mhz} to {band:n41.dl_high_mhz} MHz, used both ways.

questions.title: Welcome to the middle of the ruler
questions.text: Mid band sits between the low bands (below 1000 MHz) and the very high mmWave bands. Mid-band waves travel less far than low-band ones, but they carry more data, like a medium-sized pipe. The first mid band is "{band:B2.name}". Its downlink runs {band:B2.dl_low_mhz} to {band:B2.dl_high_mhz} MHz. B25 ("{band:B25.name}") is a bigger box that holds B2 (it ends at {band:B25.dl_high_mhz} MHz instead of {band:B2.dl_high_mhz}). Their 5G twins are n2 and n25.

questions.title: Two mid bands wait for unit 4
questions.text: n41 and n77 are mid band too. They are big 5G-only "capacity" bands, so they get their own unit later (unit 4). This unit covers the older mid bands from 4G days: PCS, AWS and WCS.
